d: The hCG level above which a normal pregnancy inside the uterus should always show a gestational sac on transvaginal ultrasound, about 1,500 to 3,500 mIU/mL.
A positive pregnancy test when ultrasound sees no pregnancy inside or outside the uterus. Repeat hCG levels and repeat imaging sort it out.

An autoimmune clotting disorder caused by antiphospholipid antibodies. It causes clots, including in the placenta, and recurrent pregnancy loss; in pregnancy it is treated with low-dose aspirin plus heparin.
A stain for a protein made only from the maternal copy of a gene. It is negative in a complete mole, which has no maternal chromosomes, and positive in a partial mole.
Tumor-like growth of trophoblast after a pregnancy, shown by an hCG that plateaus or rises. It includes invasive mole, choriocarcinoma and placental site tumor, and chemotherapy usually cures it.

Two bright rings around an early gestational sac on ultrasound, made by two layers of decidua, the pregnant uterine lining. It supports a pregnancy inside the uterus; an ectopic pseudosac has one ring.
Villi swollen with fluid into grape-like vesicles with an empty center. All villi are swollen in a complete mole; swollen and normal villi are mixed in a partial mole.
